advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass an explicit committer identity (or otherwise ensure one exists) to the auto-heal merge, and do not classify an identity/config merge failure as an S3DoctorConflict.
evidence: s3_doctor.py:209-217 `merge = _git(base_path, "merge", *extra, head_ref, "--no-edit", "-m", ...)` — no `-c user.email` / `-c user.name`
push.py:656-668 rebar's own commit path builds `identity = [-c user.name=..., -c user.email=...]` before committing
s3_doctor.py:46-52 `_git` calls run_git with default env (no identity injected)
s3_doctor.py:218-222 a non-zero merge (including a 'Committer identity unknown' failure) unconditionally raises S3DoctorConflict with an fsck-recover hint
advisory.finding: The auto-heal merge commit in _fold_heads runs git merge via s3_doctor._git with no committer identity, unlike rebar's own commit path which explicitly passes `-c user.name`/`-c user.email`. If the store repo has no configured git identity, the merge fails and is reported (misleadingly) as an S3DoctorConflict rather than an identity/config error.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Hold the write_lock across both the fold AND the bundle-create/publish so the published bundle is pinned to merged_sha, or bundle explicitly from merged_sha rather than live HEAD/branch.
evidence: s3_doctor.py:201-223 `with _lock.write_lock(...)` wraps ONLY the merge loop and returns at line 223
s3_doctor.py:132-134 `merged_sha = _fold_heads(...)` then `_publish_and_prune(...)` is called after the lock context has exited
s3_doctor.py:250 `create = _git(base_path, "bundle", "create", bundle_path, "HEAD", f"refs/heads/{ref}")` reads live HEAD/branch state with no lock held
advisory.finding: _publish_and_prune (branch -f, git bundle create from HEAD/refs/heads/<ref>, put, delete) runs OUTSIDE rebar's write_lock — the lock is released when _fold_heads' `with` block exits. A concurrent rebar writer that advances HEAD or the branch between the fold and the bundle-create can make the published bundle carry a tip different from merged_sha (or a partially-written state), breaking the lossless/crash-safe invariant.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the heal_multi_bundle call so unexpected (non-conflict, non-optional-dep) exceptions are logged and swallowed per the best-effort push contract instead of propagating.
evidence: push.py:493-511 only `except s3_doctor.S3DoctorConflict` and `except OptionalDependencyError` wrap the `heal_multi_bundle` call
push.py:8-11 module docstring: 'ALWAYS returns None (best-effort): a push failure never fails the caller'
s3_doctor.py:256/269 `s3.s3.put_object(...)` / `s3.s3.delete_object(...)` can raise arbitrary (e.g. botocore ClientError) exceptions not derived from S3DoctorConflict/OptionalDependencyError
advisory.finding: push_tickets_branch only catches S3DoctorConflict and OptionalDependencyError around the heal call; any other exception raised by heal_multi_bundle (e.g. a boto ClientError from put_object/delete_object, a git/OS error during publish, or a failure in s3remote_factory) propagates out of push_tickets_branch, violating its documented ‘ALWAYS returns None (best-effort): a push failure never fails the caller’ contract.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make fake_git keep returning the multi-bundle signature after the heal, and assert heals==1 (guard prevents a second heal) so removing `healed_once` fails the test.
evidence: push.py:490 `if _is_multi_bundle(stderr) and not healed_once:` then push.py:511-512 `healed_once = True; continue`
test_s3_doctor_heldout.py:306-312 fake_git returns success once heals!=0, so a persistent multi-bundle is never simulated
test_s3_doctor_heldout.py:327 `assert state["heals"] == 1, "heal must fire exactly once (healed_once guard)"` — still passes if the guard is removed, since the retry converges
dropped.finding: test_push_invokes_heal_once_then_converges is regression-blind to the `healed_once` guard it claims to pin. Because fake_git returns success on the second push (when state['heals']!=0), removing the `healed_once` guard entirely would still leave heals==1 (heal fires once, then the push converges and the loop returns) — the assertion cannot detect loss of the guard. The guard's real contract (do NOT re-invoke heal when the push STILL reports multi-bundle) is never exercised.
scenarios: A refactor removes or inverts the `healed_once` guard; heal would re-fire on a persistently multi-bundle remote (infinite heal->retry loop) but the test still passes
